summary.text: Terry Meza is a Democratic state representative from Texas who has represented District 105 since 2019 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Meza is a former teacher and the owner of a law practice.

paragraphs.text: Terry Meza graduated from Irving High School and studied at the University of Texas at Arlington, the University of Dallas and Texas Wesleyan University.
Her career experience includes working as a teacher at South Grand Prairie High School and owning a law practice.
Meza assumed office in the Texas House on January 8, 2019, succeeding Rodney Anderson, a Republican.
In 2023 and 2024 she was assigned to the Environmental Regulation Committee and the International Relations & Economic Development Committee.
She won re-election in 2024, defeating Republican Rose Cannaday.
In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey, Meza described herself as a fourth-generation resident of Irving, an educator and a small business owner who has run her own law practice since 2000.
She said her campaign priorities included accepting federal Medicaid money to expand health coverage, rebuilding public schools and supporting working families.
